## 🎯 Exemple 1: Global Translation Orchestrator (PARALLEL)

**Use Case**: Traduire un document dans 15 langues instantanément
**Strategy**: Parallel (indépendant)
**Speedup**: 15x (15 × 20min → 20min)

### COMMAND Structure

```yaml
# .claude/commands/translate-global.md
---
description: Orchestrate parallel translation to multiple languages
allowed-tools: Task, AskUserQuestion, Bash(git)
---

## 1️⃣ PARSE ARGUMENTS

Extract inputs:
- `content_file`: Path to markdown/text file
- `languages`: List of target languages (en, es, fr, de, it, ja, zh, ko, ru, ar, pt, nl, pl, sv, tr)
- `glossary`: Optional glossary file for consistency

Example:
/translate-global docs/README.md [es,fr,de,it,ja,zh,ko] --glossary docs/glossary.json

## 2️⃣ VALIDATE INPUTS

Verify requirements:
- Content file exists and readable (max 50KB)
- All language codes valid (ISO 639-1)
- Glossary valid JSON if provided
- No duplicate languages

If missing/unclear, use AskUserQuestion:
- Ask for content source (file path or paste text)
- Ask for target languages (provide dropdown)
- Ask for glossary requirement (optional)

## 3️⃣ ORCHESTRATE (PARALLEL STRATEGY)

Launch translator agents **concurrently** for each language:

Task(
  subagent_type="translator-spanish",
  description="Translate to Spanish",
  prompt="Translate the following content to Spanish using professional tone. Use glossary if provided for consistency."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="translator-french",
  description="Translate to French",
  prompt="Translate the following content to French using professional tone. Use glossary if provided for consistency."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="translator-german",
  description="Translate to German",
  prompt="Translate the following content to German using professional tone. Use glossary if provided for consistency."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="translator-italian",
  description="Translate to Italian",
  prompt="Translate the following content to Italian using professional tone. Use glossary if provided for consistency."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="translator-japanese",
  description="Translate to Japanese",
  prompt="Translate the following content to Japanese using professional tone. Use glossary if provided for consistency."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="translator-mandarin",
  description="Translate to Mandarin",
  prompt="Translate the following content to Mandarin (Simplified) using professional tone. Use glossary if provided for consistency."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="translator-korean",
  description="Translate to Korean",
  prompt="Translate the following content to Korean using professional tone. Use glossary if provided for consistency."
)

# ... 8 more languages ...

⚡ PARALLEL EXECUTION: All 15 agents run simultaneously
Expected time: ~20 minutes (vs 300 minutes sequential)

## 4️⃣ AGGREGATE RESULTS

Collect translations from all 15 agents:
- Spanish: ✅ (2450 words)
- French: ✅ (2380 words)
- German: ✅ (2680 words)
- ... (all others)

Total: 15/15 translations complete ✅

## 5️⃣ REPORT TO USER

Summary:
- ✅ Translations: 15/15 complete
- 📊 Total words: 35,280
- ⏱️ Time: 20 minutes
- 💰 Cost: $45 (vs manual cost ~$1,500)
- 🚀 Speedup: 15x
- 📁 Output: s3://translations/README/{language}.md

```

### Key Points

✅ **DO**:
- Launch all translator agents in **parallel**
- No dependencies between languages
- Each agent handles one language independently
- Aggregate all results together

❌ **DON'T**:
- Translate sequentially (would take 300 min)
- Have one translator dependency-chain
- Execute translation tasks directly (let agents do it)
- Parse/validate each translation (agents handle this)

## 📦 Exemple 2: CI/CD Pipeline Orchestrator (SEQUENTIAL)

**Use Case**: Automated build, test, deploy with quality gates
**Strategy**: Sequential (dépendances strictes)
**Phases**: Build → Test → Deploy (each phase blocks until success)

### COMMAND Structure

```yaml
# .claude/commands/ci-cd-pipeline.md
---
description: Orchestrate sequential CI/CD pipeline with quality gates
allowed-tools: Task, AskUserQuestion, Bash(git)
---

## 1️⃣ PARSE ARGUMENTS

Extract inputs:
- `branch`: Git branch to deploy (default: main)
- `environment`: staging or production
- `rollback`: Auto-rollback on health check failure? (yes/no)

Example:
/ci-cd-pipeline --branch feature/auth --env staging --rollback yes

## 2️⃣ VALIDATE INPUTS

Verify requirements:
- Branch exists in git
- No uncommitted changes on branch
- Environment config valid
- Deployment credentials available

Use AskUserQuestion if missing:
- Confirm branch to deploy
- Confirm target environment (staging/production)
- Confirm rollback strategy

## 3️⃣ ORCHESTRATE (SEQUENTIAL STRATEGY)

### PHASE 1: BUILD (Parallel agents, sequential phases)

Launch 2 builder agents in parallel:

Task(
  subagent_type="frontend-builder",
  description="Build frontend application",
  prompt="Run 'npm run build' in frontend/ directory. BLOCK if fails. Return artifact path."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="backend-builder",
  description="Build backend application",
  prompt="Run 'cargo build --release' in backend/ directory. BLOCK if fails. Return artifact path."
)

🚨 WAIT for both to complete AND succeed before moving to Phase 2

### PHASE 2: TEST (Parallel agents, sequential phases)

Launch 3 tester agents in parallel (only if build succeeded):

Task(
  subagent_type="unit-tester",
  description="Run unit tests",
  prompt="Run 'npm test' with coverage report. REQUIRE coverage >80%. BLOCK if fails."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="integration-tester",
  description="Run integration tests",
  prompt="Run integration test suite. BLOCK if any test fails."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="e2e-tester",
  description="Run E2E tests",
  prompt="Run E2E test suite with Playwright. BLOCK if any test fails."
)

🚨 WAIT for all to complete AND all pass >80% coverage before Phase 3

### PHASE 3: DEPLOY (Sequential agents)

Launch deployer agent (only if all tests passed):

Task(
  subagent_type="deployer",
  description="Deploy to environment",
  prompt="Deploy to {environment} with health checks. Auto-rollback if health checks fail. Report deployment status."
)

🚨 WAIT for deploy to complete

## 4️⃣ AGGREGATE RESULTS

Collect metrics from all phases:

**Phase 1 - Build**:
- Frontend: ✅ (2.3 MB artifact)
- Backend: ✅ (15.7 MB binary)

**Phase 2 - Test**:
- Unit tests: ✅ (847 passed, 0 failed, coverage 87%)
- Integration tests: ✅ (142 passed, 0 failed)
- E2E tests: ✅ (45 passed, 0 failed)

**Phase 3 - Deploy**:
- Pre-deploy backup: ✅
- Deployment: ✅ (3 regions)
- Health checks: ✅ (all green)

Total: 8/8 phases complete ✅

## 5️⃣ REPORT TO USER

Summary:
- ✅ Pipeline: SUCCESS
- 🏗️ Phase 1 (Build): ✅ (Frontend + Backend)
- 🧪 Phase 2 (Test): ✅ (Unit + Integration + E2E)
  - Coverage: 87% (target: >80%)
  - Tests: 1034 passed, 0 failed
- 🚀 Phase 3 (Deploy): ✅ (3 regions)
  - Health: All green
  - Rollback: Enabled
- ⏱️ Total time: 60 minutes
- 💰 Cost: $15 (vs manual $100+)
- 📊 Details: [Full Report Link]

```

### Key Points

✅ **DO**:
- Run phases **sequentially** (Phase 2 only after Phase 1 success)
- Use **quality gates** (block if tests fail, coverage <80%)
- **Parallelize within phases** (2 builders, 3 testers in parallel)
- Auto-rollback on health check failure

❌ **DON'T**:
- Run all phases in parallel (dependencies!)
- Skip quality gates
- Deploy without tests
- Execute build/test tasks directly

## 🌍 Exemple 3: Batch Localization Orchestrator (BATCH)

**Use Case**: Generate 174 locale files for global app
**Strategy**: Batch (large dataset)
**Batch Size**: 20 items per wave
**Total Waves**: 9 waves (174 ÷ 20 = 8.7 → 9)

### COMMAND Structure

```yaml
# .claude/commands/generate-locales.md
---
description: Orchestrate batch generation of locale files (174 locales)
allowed-tools: Task, AskUserQuestion, Bash(git)
---

## 1️⃣ PARSE ARGUMENTS

Extract inputs:
- `source_locale`: Base locale file (default: en-US.json)
- `locales_file`: List of target locales
- `format`: json or yaml (default: json)

Example:
/generate-locales --source config/locales/en-US.json --format json

## 2️⃣ VALIDATE INPUTS

Verify requirements:
- Source locale file exists and valid
- Locales list has 174+ entries
- Output directory writable
- Format valid (json or yaml)

## 3️⃣ ORCHESTRATE (BATCH STRATEGY)

Total: 174 locales
Batch size: 20 locales per wave
Waves: 9 waves

### WAVE 1 (Locales 1-20: en-AU, en-CA, en-GB, en-NZ, es-ES, es-MX, es-AR, es-CO, es-CL, es-PE, fr-FR, fr-CA, fr-BE, fr-CH, de-DE, de-AT, de-CH, it-IT, pt-BR, pt-PT)

Launch 20 locale-generator agents in **parallel**:

Task(
  subagent_type="locale-generator",
  description="Generate en-AU locale",
  prompt="Generate locale file for en-AU from source. Follow naming convention."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="locale-generator",
  description="Generate en-CA locale",
  prompt="Generate locale file for en-CA from source. Follow naming convention."
)

# ... 18 more locales in parallel ...

Task(
  subagent_type="locale-generator",
  description="Generate pt-PT locale",
  prompt="Generate locale file for pt-PT from source. Follow naming convention."
)

🚨 WAIT for Wave 1 completion
✅ Wave 1: 20/20 success

### WAVE 2 (Locales 21-40: ja-JP, ja-KY, zh-CN, zh-TW, zh-HK, ko-KR, ru-RU, ar-SA, tr-TR, pl-PL, nl-NL, sv-SE, da-DK, no-NO, fi-FI, et-EE, lt-LT, lv-LV, el-GR, hu-HU)

Launch 20 locale-generator agents in **parallel**:

Task(...) × 20 agents

🚨 WAIT for Wave 2 completion
✅ Wave 2: 20/20 success

### WAVE 3-8

Repeat for waves 3-8 (each with 20 locales)

### WAVE 9 (Locales 161-174: hi-IN, bn-IN, th-TH, vi-VN, id-ID, my-MM, lo-LA, km-KH, ta-IN, te-IN, kn-IN, ml-IN, ur-PK, sr-RS)

Launch 14 locale-generator agents in **parallel**:

Task(...) × 14 agents

🚨 WAIT for Wave 9 completion
✅ Wave 9: 14/14 success

## 4️⃣ AGGREGATE RESULTS

Aggregate results from all 9 waves:

Wave 1: 20/20 ✅
Wave 2: 20/20 ✅
Wave 3: 20/20 ✅
Wave 4: 20/20 ✅
Wave 5: 20/20 ✅
Wave 6: 20/20 ✅
Wave 7: 20/20 ✅
Wave 8: 20/20 ✅
Wave 9: 14/14 ✅

Total: 174/174 ✅

## 5️⃣ REPORT TO USER

Summary:
- ✅ Locales generated: 174/174
- 📊 Total files: 174
- 📦 Batch size: 20 per wave
- 🌊 Waves: 9 (8 full + 1 partial)
- ⏱️ Time: 3.5 hours
  - Per wave: ~25 minutes
- 💰 Cost: $85 (vs manual $2,500+)
- 🚀 Speedup: 10x
- 📁 Output: locales/generated/{locale}.json

```

### Key Points

✅ **DO**:
- Split large datasets into **batches** (20 items/wave)
- Run each wave **in parallel**
- **Wait between waves** (validate before next)
- Stop on errors and report which wave failed

❌ **DON'T**:
- Launch all 174 agents at once (would timeout)
- Sequence all 174 (would take 1,000+ hours)
- Skip error checking between waves
- Generate without validation

## 🎯 Exemple 4: Multi-Agent Workflow (CONDITIONAL)

**Use Case**: Content processing with dynamic routing
**Strategy**: Conditional (runtime decisions)
**Flow**: Analyze → Route based on type → Process → Review

### COMMAND Structure

```yaml
# .claude/commands/process-content.md
---
description: Orchestrate conditional content processing based on type
allowed-tools: Task, AskUserQuestion, Bash(git)
---

## 1️⃣ PARSE ARGUMENTS

Extract inputs:
- `content`: Text, image, or video file
- `content_type`: auto-detect or specify (text, image, video)

## 2️⃣ VALIDATE INPUTS

Verify file exists and is supported format.

## 3️⃣ ORCHESTRATE (CONDITIONAL STRATEGY)

### Step 1: ANALYZE content type

Task(
  subagent_type="analyzer",
  description="Analyze content type",
  prompt="Determine if content is text, image, or video. Return: {type, size, duration}"
)

🚨 WAIT for analysis result

### Step 2: ROUTE based on type

If type == "text":

Task(
  subagent_type="text-processor",
  description="Process text content",
  prompt="Extract entities, sentiment, keywords. Return structured output."
)

If type == "image":

Task(
  subagent_type="image-processor",
  description="Process image",
  prompt="Analyze image: objects, text, scene. Check quality. Return analysis."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="ocr-processor",
  description="Extract text from image",
  prompt="Run OCR if image contains text. Return extracted text."
)

If type == "video":

Task(
  subagent_type="video-processor",
  description="Process video",
  prompt="Analyze: duration, quality, objects. Return analysis."
)

Task(
  subagent_type="transcription-processor",
  description="Transcribe audio",
  prompt="Transcribe audio track if duration >5 min. Return transcript."
)

### Step 3: REVIEW

Task(
  subagent_type="reviewer",
  description="Review and validate output",
  prompt="Quality check all extracted data. Validate completeness. Return review report."
)

## 4️⃣ AGGREGATE RESULTS

Collect results from routing path + review.

## 5️⃣ REPORT TO USER

Summary with:
- Content type identified
- Agents executed (conditional path)
- All outputs
- Quality validation result
```

### Key Points

✅ **DO**:
- **Analyze first** to make routing decision
- Use conditional logic to **launch agents dynamically**
- **Wait for decision** before launching next phase
- Support multiple input types

❌ **DON'T**:
- Launch all agents upfront (waste resources)
- Hard-code processing path
- Skip analysis step

## 📋 Implementation Checklist

Use this checklist when creating a new COMMAND orchestrator:

```
PARSING:
  ☐ Extract all required arguments
  ☐ Set sensible defaults
  ☐ Handle multiple input formats

VALIDATION:
  ☐ Verify all inputs exist
  ☐ Check format/structure
  ☐ Use AskUserQuestion for missing data

ORCHESTRATION:
  ☐ Choose strategy (Parallel/Sequential/Batch)
  ☐ Write clear Task() descriptions
  ☐ Add comments for phase boundaries
  ☐ Include wait points and quality gates

AGGREGATION:
  ☐ Collect all agent outputs
  ☐ Check success/failure counts
  ☐ Handle errors gracefully

REPORTING:
  ☐ Success count ✅
  ☐ Failure count ❌
  ☐ Time metrics ⏱️
  ☐ Cost metrics 💰
  ☐ Speedup calculation 🚀
  ☐ Output location 📁
```
